page.layout: One page of verse, one column, centred under the running head. Page number top right. Signature mark at the foot, right.

p.i: Auster fatiscentes procella fauciet Puppes frementi in æquore. Immurmuret fretis Aquilo Britannicis, Remisque remos atterat. Tenere clavum ipsos Noti nautas vetent; Tenere cursum nox vetet: Nec sint amiciora Iberis æquora Ægyptio quàm militi, Quum rex Pharius viros, rabiem, currus, equos In gentem Hebræam verteret. Heu, quanta tempestas polo à Britannico, Medina Dux, tibi imminet! Lethalis inquinabit, heu! sudor tuos Vanusq; pallor remiges. Quid eiulatus non virilis? quid frequens Indicta[?] supplicatio? Quid templa & aras, quid precibus cælum iuvat Onerasse, Ibere Carnifex? Quid facta vota littoralibus Dijs Reditu super & victoria? Annon Draconem respicis quantus ruat Ille, & celer rates sequi, Ille impavidus subire mortem pro fide, Deique nostri gloria? Dracone, quem regina classi praficit, An ullus est peritior? Seu nauticus sit edomandus impetus, Pedestris aut exercitus?

page.notes: Page number "23" is partly unclear in the scan; read as 23 with a doubtful final stroke. "Indicta" has a doubtful letter in the ct ligature. "Ibere" and "Deique" are printed as seen, with no accent beyond what is visible. The verse is printed as one stanza, lines run together with spaces. Printed spellings kept: "fauciet", "eiulatus", "rates", "Dijs", "Vanusq;", "Ibere". Signature "B. iij." is printed at the foot, not in the text.
